question: Approaching a railroad crossing without active warning signals, a driver should:
options: a:Slow down, look both ways, and listen before crossing,b:Proceed normally if no train is visible,c:Rely only on the crossbuck sign and keep speed
note: If a crossing has no warning devices, slow down, look both directions, and listen for trains before proceeding.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a posted speed limit sign represent?
options: a:The maximum legal speed under ideal road and weather conditions.,b:A recommended speed you may ignore if traffic is light.,c:The exact speed you must travel at all times to avoid a ticket.,d:A minimum speed you must maintain.
note: Speed limits indicate the maximum legal speed under ideal conditions; drivers must slow down when conditions are less than ideal.

question: What is the most common color used for warning signs?
options: a:Yellow.,b:Red.,c:Green.
note: Most warning signs are yellow (diamond-shaped) with black symbols or lettering to warn of potential hazards.

question: If you are following a school bus or a tank truck carrying flammable liquids, you should be prepared to do what?
options: a:Pass them cautiously on the right,b:Decrease your following distance,c:Be prepared to stop at all railroad crossings
note: School buses and tank trucks carrying flammable liquids must stop at all railroad crossings; be prepared to stop when following them.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: From which lane must you make a left turn when leaving a one-way street?
options: a:The lane nearest the left curb.,b:The lane nearest the center of the street.,c:The lane nearest the right curb.,d:Any lane as long as you signal.
note: On a one-way street, make a left turn from the lane closest to the left curb into the nearest lawful lane.

question: How should you change lanes?
options: a:Gradually and carefully after checking mirrors and blind spots,b:Quickly and often to stay ahead of traffic,c:Only when a car is in your blind spot
note: Change lanes gradually and carefully; check mirrors, signals, and blind spots before moving over.

question: What does a double solid yellow centerline indicate about passing?
options: a:Passing is not allowed from either direction.,b:Passing is allowed from both directions.,c:Passing is allowed only from your direction of travel.
note: A double solid yellow line means traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is prohibited both ways.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is likely to happen if you drive substantially slower than the flow of traffic?
options: a:You may interfere with traffic flow and could be cited.,b:You will improve traffic flow.,c:You will automatically be demonstrating defensive driving.
note: If you block the reasonable movement of traffic by driving too slowly, you can be cited. Match the flow when safe and legal.

question: Which headlights should you use when driving in fog, heavy rain, or snow?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Only fog lights and no headlights.,d:Parking lights only.
note: Low beams should be used in fog, rain, or snow because high beams create glare and reduce visibility.

question: Alcohol consumption affects driving by:
options: a:Slowing reflexes and reaction time,b:Waking you up,c:Improving concentration
note: Alcohol is a depressant that slows brain activity, reflexes, and judgment needed for safe driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you pass another vehicle?
options: a:When the centerline next to your lane is broken and it is safe to do so.,b:When you are on a hill or curve and cannot see ahead.,c:When the centerline next to your lane is solid.
note: Passing is allowed when the broken centerline is adjacent to your lane and there is no oncoming traffic and it's safe.

question: How do sudden gusts of wind affect vehicles on highways?
options: a:They can cause problems for all vehicles, not just large ones.,b:They only affect the movement of very large trucks.,c:They only reduce visibility but do not affect vehicle stability.,d:They pose no risk on modern highways.
note: Strong crosswinds can affect small and large vehicles, reducing stability and visibility; all drivers should adjust accordingly.

question: Are drivers required to yield to pedestrians even if the pedestrian is crossing against the light?
options: a:True,b:False
note: You must yield right-of-way to pedestrians even if they misjudge signals or cross against a light.

question: At what approximate speed can a car begin to hydroplane on standing water?
options: a:About 35 miles per hour.,b:About 45 miles per hour.,c:About 40 miles per hour.,d:About 25 miles per hour.
note: Hydroplaning can begin at speeds near 35 mph because tires cannot channel water away effectively above that speed, causing loss of road contact.

question: When approaching an accident scene, what is the appropriate action if you are not involved?
options: a:Keep driving and maintain attention to the road; do not stop unless you are involved or emergency help hasn't arrived.,b:Stop immediately to watch and take photos.,c:Drive toward the scene to offer assistance without checking for hazards.
note: Do not stop at a crash scene unless involved or emergency services haven't arrived; keep moving while watching for people and hazards.

question: What is a good practice when driving near a large commercial vehicle?
options: a:Drive beside it for long stretches to stay out of its blind spot.,b:Avoid lingering beside it — do not stay in its blind spots.,c:Tailgate to reduce wind drag on your vehicle.,d:Always pass on the right regardless of conditions.
note: Large commercial vehicles have large blind spots on each side; avoid riding beside them for long periods and pass quickly and safely.

question: What is the best general way to reduce the chance of hydroplaning in wet weather?
options: a:Slow down to speeds appropriate for wet conditions.,b:Maintain the same speed you use on dry roads.,c:Brake hard as soon as you feel the car slide.,d:Drive in the center of the road at high speed.
note: Drive slower in wet conditions; lower speeds help tires channel water and maintain road contact.

question: How should you prepare when driving to an unfamiliar area?
options: a:Plan your route before you start driving.,b:Depend mainly on road signs while driving.,c:Drive with only a general sense of the destination.
note: Plan trips in advance and check maps or directions so you aren't driving with only a vague idea of the route.

question: If a truck or bus is making a right turn where you also need to turn right, what should you do?
options: a:Wait until the truck or bus completes its turn before you turn.,b:Try to turn quickly before it completes its turn.,c:Squeeze between the vehicle and the curb to get through.
note: Large vehicles need extra space to turn; do not try to squeeze between them and the curb or you may collide.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do before making a turn?
options: a:Signal three to four seconds before turning.,b:Turn the wheel immediately without signaling.,c:Increase your speed to clear the turn quickly.
note: Activate your turn signal several seconds before the turn to inform others of your intentions.

question: If you discover a vehicle defect that affects safety, when should you repair it?
options: a:Correct the defect as soon as possible, before driving further.,b:Wait until you can afford it.,c:Drive more slowly to compensate for the defect.
note: Any safety-related defect should be repaired promptly to ensure safe vehicle operation.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a right turn, what should you avoid doing?
options: a:Turning too wide so you leave your lane.,b:Signaling to other drivers.,c:Slowing down before the turn.
note: Do not turn too wide on a right turn. Signal and slow down properly before turning.

question: Because motorcycles, scooters, and mopeds can be hard to see, drivers should:
options: a:Make regular visual checks and be especially alert.,b:Share the same lane with them.,c:Slow to a complete stop whenever they are nearby.
note: Motorcycles are small and can be hidden in blind spots; constantly check and be vigilant for them.

question: When backing up, how should you position yourself to see properly?
options: a:Look through the rear window by placing your right arm on the passenger seat and turning to look back.,b:Rely only on mirrors.,c:Press the gas lightly while backing to maintain momentum.
note: When reversing, turn and look through the rear window; do not depend solely on mirrors and back up slowly.

question: If you park facing uphill on a street with a curb, you should set the parking brake and:
options: a:Turn the front wheels toward the curb.,b:Turn the front wheels away from the curb.,c:Leave the wheels pointing straight ahead.,d:Turn the wheels toward the centerline.
note: When parking uphill at a curb, turn wheels away from the curb so the vehicle will roll into the curb rather than into traffic if it moves.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You arrive at an intersection with a flashing red light. What should you do?
options: a:Slow down and cross if it feels clear.,b:Come to a full stop, yield, and proceed when safe.,c:Only stop if other cars are present.,d:Treat it as a flashing yellow light.
note: A flashing red signal is equivalent to a stop sign: stop completely, yield to others, then go when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If traffic ahead is blocking an intersection, what is the correct action?
options: a:Wait to enter the intersection until you can fully cross it,b:Use your horn to urge traffic to move,c:Drive closely behind the vehicle ahead in case the light changes
note: Do not enter an intersection unless you can fully clear it; otherwise you may be cited for blocking it.

question: How is alcohol classified in terms of its effect on the body?
options: a:A depressant.,b:A stimulant.,c:An antihistamine.
note: Alcohol is a depressant that slows brain and body functions, impairing judgment and reflexes.

question: Fatigue while driving increases the risk of:
options: a:Falling asleep behind the wheel and crashing,b:Missing an exit only,c:Arriving earlier to appointments
note: Fatigue impairs judgment and reaction time and can lead to falling asleep at the wheel and a crash.

question: Signs that require drivers to obey a rule (such as speed limits or parking restrictions) are called:
options: a:Regulatory signs.,b:Warning signs.,c:Information signs.,d:Guide signs.
note: Regulatory signs tell drivers what they must or must not do; failure to comply is enforceable by penalty.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes, what should you do to check for traffic in your blind spot?
options: a:Rely only on your mirrors.,b:Look over your shoulder toward the lane you plan to enter.,c:Trust the rearview mirror exclusively.,d:Rely on the vehicle's blind-spot sensor only.
note: Glance over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move to check blind spots; mirrors alone do not show everything.

question: If you see heavy smoke covering the roadway ahead, what should you do?
options: a:Reduce speed, move as far right as possible, and stop off the roadway until it is safe.,b:Turn on four-way flashers and drive through quickly.,c:Turn on high beam headlights to see better.,d:Continue at the same speed and stay in your lane.
note: If smoke obscures the road, slow down, pull to the right, and stop off the roadway until conditions improve; some smoke can be hazardous to breathe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your interstate exit, you should:
options: a:Continue to the next exit and not attempt dangerous maneuvers to return,b:Quickly cut across traffic to reach the exit,c:Make a U-turn on the freeway
note: Do not make last-minute turns or U-turns on an interstate; go to the next exit safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before changing lanes on a multi-lane highway, what should you do?
options: a:Check mirrors and blind spots and signal; do not sound your horn or flash headlights.,b:Sound your horn to warn other drivers.,c:Turn on your headlights to signal intent.
note: Check rearview and side mirrors, look over your shoulder for blind spots, and signal before changing lanes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it permitted to pass another vehicle on the right shoulder?
options: a:Never,b:When the car ahead is driving too slowly,c:When the car ahead is signaling a left turn
note: You must not drive off the pavement or onto the shoulder to pass another vehicle; passing on the right is only allowed where it is legal and safe.

question: To reduce glare from an approaching vehicle's headlights, what should you do?
options: a:Look briefly toward the right side of the road and then resume scanning.,b:Stare at the centerline to judge distance.,c:Flash your high beams back at them.
note: Glance toward the right edge of the road to avoid being blinded, then resume scanning ahead to maintain lane position.

question: If you are facing a green traffic light but pedestrians are in the intersection, what must you do?
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to the pedestrians.,b:Proceed because you have the green light.,c:Honk and expect pedestrians to get out of the way.,d:Speed up to clear the crosswalk before they finish crossing.
note: Even on a green signal you must yield to pedestrians already in the intersection or crosswalk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto a freeway, you should be driving:
options: a:At or near the speed of the traffic already on the freeway,b:Five to ten mph below freeway traffic speed,c:Well below the posted speed to be cautious
note: Enter the freeway at about the same speed as traffic so you can merge safely; always yield to traffic on the freeway.

question: A person using a white cane or guide dog is likely to be:
options: a:A blind or visually impaired person,b:A participant in a traffic study,c:A deaf person
note: Pedestrians using a white cane or guide dog are blind or visually impaired and must be yielded to at all times.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a roadway from a private road or driveway, what must you do?
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians and vehicles already on the roadway.,b:Blow your horn to warn approaching cars.,c:Partially enter the roadway to alert other drivers.
note: You must yield to pedestrians and traffic on the roadway when entering from a private road or driveway.

question: How far ahead should you look while driving to anticipate problems?
options: a:One minute ahead.,b:45 seconds ahead.,c:15 to 20 seconds ahead.,d:Five seconds ahead.
note: Look 15 to 20 seconds ahead (roughly one city block at moderate speed) to see hazards and plan maneuvers.

question: When meeting an oncoming vehicle at night, which headlight setting should you use?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Turn off headlights and use parking lights.
note: Do not use high beams when approaching or following another vehicle; use low beams to avoid blinding other drivers.

question: Like alcohol and drugs, what effect can drowsiness have on driving?
options: a:It can impair judgment and slow reaction time.,b:It improves alertness.,c:It has no effect on driving judgment.
note: Lack of sleep reduces reaction time, awareness, and judgment, similar to impairment from drugs or alcohol.

question: Is it legal to drink alcoholic beverages in a vehicle on a public road?
options: a:No — consuming or possessing an open alcoholic beverage on a public road is prohibited.,b:Yes, as long as you are not driving.,c:Yes, if you sit in the back of a pickup truck.
note: It's illegal to consume or possess an open alcoholic beverage on public roads; open containers in driver/passenger areas are prohibited.

question: What should you do before driving if you are taking any medication?
options: a:Consult your doctor or pharmacist about how it may affect your driving.,b:Have someone follow you home to monitor you.,c:Keep the window open and drive more slowly without consulting anyone.
note: Legal medications can impair driving ability. Ask a healthcare professional about side effects and driving safety.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under which condition may you legally pass another vehicle?
options: a:When the centerline next to your lane is a broken yellow line and it is safe to pass.,b:While on a hill or in a curve where visibility is limited.,c:By driving onto the highway shoulder to get around a slow car.,d:When your lane is next to a solid yellow line regardless of visibility.
note: You may pass when the centerline next to your lane is a broken yellow line and it is safe to complete the pass. Do not pass on hills, curves, on the shoulder, or over solid yellow lines.

question: Who may park in parking spaces reserved for persons with disabilities?
options: a:Only vehicles displaying special license plates or disabled parking placards,b:Any vehicle if the driver is visiting someone nearby,c:Any vehicle if the space appears empty
note: A space marked for persons with disabilities may be used only by vehicles displaying appropriate disabled license plates or placards.

question: Which of the following does stopping distance NOT depend on?
options: a:The time of day.,b:Your reaction time.,c:The condition of your vehicle's brakes.,d:The condition of the roadway and tires.
note: Stopping distance depends on reaction time, vehicle and brake condition, tires, weight, speed, and road conditions — not on the time of day.

question: When driving at night, which of these actions should you take?
options: a:Always use high beams.,b:Look directly at oncoming headlights.,c:Increase your following distance.,d:Drive at the posted speed no matter what.
note: Night driving reduces visibility; increase following distance and use high/low beams correctly to avoid blinding others.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning or changing lanes, when must you signal?
options: a:Always signal your intentions, even if no other traffic is visible.,b:Only when visible traffic is present.,c:Only during nighttime driving.
note: You must always signal before turning, changing lanes, or pulling from a curb to warn other road users.

question: Which action helps prevent becoming an aggressive driver?
options: a:Relax and focus on driving rather than reacting to others.,b:Tailgate drivers who are too slow.,c:Drive above posted speed limits to get ahead.,d:Use your horn aggressively to assert your right-of-way.
note: Concentrate on safe driving, be realistic about travel time, and avoid taking other drivers' actions personally.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it appropriate to drive at the posted maximum speed limit?
options: a:Only under ideal road and weather conditions.,b:Any time you feel comfortable with that speed.,c:Only at night when traffic is lighter.,d:Only in posted school zones.
note: The posted speed is the maximum under ideal conditions; you must slow down when weather, road, or traffic conditions require.

question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light instruct drivers to do?
options: a:Proceed with caution,b:Come to a complete stop,c:Yield to all traffic then proceed only when intersection is clear
note: A flashing yellow light means slow down and proceed with caution; you do not need to stop if it is clear.

question: When should drivers yield the right-of-way to pedestrians in a crosswalk?
options: a:At all times,b:Only if the pedestrian waves,c:Only if the pedestrian is not using a phone
note: Yield to pedestrians in crosswalks; stop and allow them to cross safely before proceeding.

question: At a school crossing sign, you should:
options: a:Always stop whether a stop sign is present or not.,b:Be alert for children and be ready to stop.,c:Always sound your horn when children are nearby.,d:Speed through to clear the area quickly.
note: Pentagonal school crossing signs indicate you are approaching a school zone; be alert and prepared to stop for children.

question: If the center of the road is marked with a solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line and the broken line is beside your lane, when may you pass?
options: a:Only in an emergency.,b:Whenever traffic is clear.,c:Only during daylight.,d:Never.
note: When the broken yellow line is next to your lane, you may cross it to pass when there is no oncoming traffic and it is safe to do so.

question: When may you cross a solid yellow centerline?
options: a:Only to make a turn into or out of a driveway or side road.,b:Anytime you want to pass slow traffic.,c:During daylight hours only.,d:Whenever traffic is light.
note: Solid yellow lines are generally not to be crossed except to turn into or from driveways or side roads where permitted.

question: What do crossbuck signs indicate?
options: a:Railroad crossings — yield to trains.,b:School zones.,c:No passing zones.
note: Crossbuck signs identify railroad crossings. You must yield to approaching trains and never try to beat a train across the tracks.

question: Do pedestrians always have the right-of-way in crosswalks and at intersections?
options: a:FALSE,b:TRUE,c:Only in marked crosswalks.,d:Only when crossing during daylight.
note: Pedestrians have the right-of-way when crossing at intersections, whether the crosswalk is marked or unmarked; however, context matters and drivers must still exercise caution.

question: When someone is injured in a collision, what is the recommended action regarding moving them?
options: a:Move the injured as far away from the road as possible immediately.,b:Avoid moving the injured unless necessary for safety.,c:Insist they walk to the sidewalk.,d:Move them into a vehicle for immediate transport.
note: Do not move injured persons unless they are in immediate danger; wait for competent medical assistance unless moving is necessary to avoid further harm.

question: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline means:
options: a:Do not pass from your lane,b:Pass with caution,c:Slow down immediately
note: A solid yellow line next to your lane indicates passing is not allowed from your direction.

question: Which commonly causes traffic accidents?
options: a:Inattentive driving, excessive speed for conditions, and following too closely (all of the above),b:Only mechanical failures,c:Perfect weather conditions
note: Inattentive driving, speeding for conditions, and tailgating are major contributors to crashes.

question: Which behavior may identify an aggressive driver?
options: a:Erratic and improper lane changes,b:Having many passengers in the car,c:Driving slower than the flow of traffic
note: Aggressive drivers often make sudden, improper lane changes or other risky maneuvers; avoid challenging them.

question: What is defensive driving?
options: a:Using safe driving strategies to avoid crashes.,b:Driving aggressively to assert your right-of-way.,c:More dangerous than not driving defensively.
note: Defensive driving means adjusting your driving to conditions and others' actions to help prevent crashes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an uncontrolled intersection where vehicles arrive simultaneously, you should:
options: a:Yield to the vehicle on your right,b:Yield to the vehicle on your left,c:Proceed immediately without yielding
note: If vehicles arrive at the same time at an uncontrolled intersection, yield to the vehicle on your right.

question: Should drivers try to continually improve their driving and observation skills?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Because driving involves risk, continually improving driving and observation skills helps keep you and others safe.

question: When may you legally drive around or under a railroad crossing gate?
options: a:Never — do not go around or under a lowered or moving gate.,b:When you can clearly see both directions.,c:When the warning lights are not flashing.
note: Never drive around or under lowered gates. Only proceed once the gate is fully raised and you can see clearly both directions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you treat a flashing red traffic signal?
options: a:Treat it the same as a stop sign and proceed when safe.,b:Slow down and proceed without stopping.,c:You are traveling the wrong way, pull over.,d:Wait until it turns green before moving.
note: A flashing red light means stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians, and go only when it is safe — like a stop sign.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: True or false: If a traffic light shows both a red light and a green arrow, you may proceed in the arrow’s direction after yielding.
options: a:True,b:False,c:Only when turning right,d:Only when pedestrians are not present
note: A green arrow permits movement in the arrow direction after yielding to any traffic or pedestrians in the intersection, regardless of a red circular light.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before passing another vehicle you should:
options: a:Check your mirrors and blind spots and signal before changing lanes,b:Honk aggressively to warn the other driver,c:Re-enter your lane within 10 feet of the passed vehicle
note: Check mirrors, blind spots, and signal before changing lanes; re-enter only when it is safe.

question: True or false: You should use high-beam headlights when driving in fog to increase visibility.
options: a:True,b:False,c:Only on unfamiliar roads,d:Only if no other cars are present
note: In fog, use low-beam headlights; high beams reflect back from fog and reduce visibility.

question: When merging onto an interstate from an entrance ramp, you should:
options: a:Stop before merging and yield to traffic.,b:Reduce speed to 25 mph and then enter the lane.,c:Accelerate to match the speed of traffic and merge when safe.,d:Assume other drivers will move over for you.
note: Use the acceleration lane to reach a speed that matches traffic on the interstate and merge smoothly when there is a safe gap.

question: For drivers age 21 or older, it is illegal to drive with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of at least:
options: a:0.05 percent.,b:0.08 percent.,c:0.02 percent.,d:0.10 percent.
note: For drivers 21 and older, operating a vehicle with a BAC of 0.08% or higher is illegal.

question: When approaching railroad tracks, what should you do?
options: a:Look and listen, slow down, and be prepared to stop.,b:Speed up to beat a potential train.,c:Try to drive around a lowered gate.
note: Always look and listen for trains, slow down, and be ready to stop if necessary when approaching tracks.

question: You must yield to a pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog:
options: a:At all times,b:Only when the guide dog is leading them,c:Only if a crossing guard is present
note: Pedestrians using a white cane or guide dog must be given the right-of-way at all times.

question: What type of information do blue roadside signs provide?
options: a:Motorist services, like rest areas and hospitals.,b:Construction and maintenance warnings.,c:Distance and directional mileage.
note: Blue signs are service signs that indicate available motorist services such as food, gas, or medical facilities.

question: During poor weather, how long should your following distance be at minimum?
options: a:Two seconds.,b:Three seconds.,c:Four seconds.,d:One second.
note: Increase following distance in bad weather; a minimum of four seconds is recommended under poor weather and traffic conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: The space you need to cross traffic safely depends on which factors?
options: a:Your vehicle's color only.,b:Road and weather conditions and oncoming traffic.,c:Whether you used your turn signals.,d:Only on the presence of a stop sign.
note: The amount of space needed to cross depends on road and weather conditions and the speed and distance of oncoming traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle traveling in the same direction, what is the correct approach?
options: a:Pass as safely and as quickly as possible, then return to your lane when it is safe.,b:Pass at the same speed as the other vehicle and stay alongside it.,c:Pass as slowly as possible to maintain visibility.,d:Pass on the shoulder if it's clear.
note: When passing, do so promptly and safely, and return to your lane only when a safe gap exists.

question: If you see orange construction signs and cones on a freeway, what should you be prepared for?
options: a:Workers and equipment ahead; slow down and be ready to stop.,b:That the lane ends immediately; speed up.,c:To change lanes and keep your current speed.
note: Work zone signs warn of workers, equipment, and lane closures — reduce speed and be prepared for delays.

question: If you are waiting in an intersection to make a left turn, how should you position your wheels?
options: a:Signal and keep your wheels turned left.,b:Signal and keep your wheels straight while waiting.,c:Flash your headlights to warn others.,d:Turn wheels sharply to the right.
note: Keep wheels straight while waiting to turn left so a rear-end collision will not push you into oncoming traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle, you should move back into the right lane when:
options: a:You are one vehicle length ahead of the passed vehicle.,b:You can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,c:You have signaled for at least three seconds.,d:You are half a car length ahead.
note: Return to the driving lane only when you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror, ensuring a safe gap.

question: Which action helps reduce road rage?
options: a:Always signal before changing lanes,b:Use the horn frequently to express frustration,c:Talk on your phone to calm down while driving
note: Signaling and obeying rules helps prevent misunderstandings that can lead to road rage.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an uncontrolled intersection where two vehicles arrive at the same time, which vehicle has the right-of-way?
options: a:The vehicle that arrives first.,b:The vehicle approaching from the right.,c:The vehicle approaching from the left.,d:The larger vehicle.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection of similar roads, the driver must yield to the vehicle on the right.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your freeway exit, what should you do?
options: a:Continue to the next exit and use it to return; do not back up on the freeway or shoulder.,b:Back up on the shoulder to reach the exit.,c:Immediately stop and reverse into the exit lane.
note: Do not back up on the freeway or shoulder. Proceed to the next exit and return to your intended route.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you see a 'Merging traffic' sign on a freeway, how should you react?
options: a:Make room for entering vehicles by changing lanes if it is safe to do so.,b:Always remain at your current speed and lane position.,c:Honk at merging drivers to warn them away.,d:Speed up aggressively to avoid merging traffic.
note: On multi-lane roads, create space for merging vehicles by moving over when safe; this helps traffic flow and reduces conflicts.

question: When must you stop at a railroad crossing?
options: a:When directed by a flagger, by a stop sign, or when flashing red signals and gates are operating.,b:Only if you see a train approaching.,c:Only at crossings with flashing lights.,d:Never — only trains stop.
note: Stop when directed by a flagger or stop sign and whenever flashing lights and gates are operating; not all crossings have active warning devices.

question: What message appears on a red octagon-shaped sign?
options: a:Do not enter.,b:One-way.,c:Stop.,d:Yield.
note: An octagon-shaped sign (eight sides) always means STOP; you must come to a complete stop at this sign.

question: How can you help prevent hydroplaning when the road is wet?
options: a:Use cruise control to maintain steady speed.,b:Slow down and avoid sudden maneuvers.,c:Immediately move to the shoulder when it starts to rain.,d:Drive in the deepest water to keep tires submerged.
note: Hydroplaning is caused by too much speed on a wet surface; slow down and drive cautiously to avoid losing traction.

question: Which of the following is a way alcohol affects driving?
options: a:It slows reaction time, impairs thinking, and gives false confidence.,b:It improves coordination and balance.,c:It increases alertness and judgment.
note: Alcohol impairs inhibition, judgment, reaction time, coordination, and vision, and may give a misleading feeling of confidence.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A practical rule for passing other vehicles is to:
options: a:Drive with the flow of traffic and pass only when needed,b:Pass on the right whenever possible,c:Always try to get to the front of slow-moving traffic
note: Passing increases collision risk; drive with traffic flow and only pass when necessary.

question: True or false: Nighttime is the safest time for cyclists to ride.
options: a:True,b:False,c:Only on well-lit streets,d:Only with high-visibility gear
note: Bicyclists are harder to see at night even with lights and reflectors; both drivers and cyclists should be extra cautious after dark.

question: Are you required to yield to children playing in the street?
options: a:True — you must exercise caution and yield to children.,b:False — children must yield to vehicles.
note: Drive very cautiously where children may be present, reducing speed in residential areas and near playgrounds.

question: What is the correct top-to-bottom order for traffic lights?
options: a:Red, yellow, green.,b:Red, green, yellow.,c:Green, red, yellow.,d:Yellow, red, green.
note: The standard vertical order is red on top, yellow in the middle, and green at the bottom.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A driver entering public traffic from a driveway or private road should:
options: a:Yield to vehicles already on the roadway,b:Expect others to stop for them,c:Force their way into traffic
note: When entering traffic from a driveway or private road, yield to drivers already using the public road.

question: How should you drive on gravel or dirt roads compared with pavement?
options: a:Slow down because tires have less traction and stopping distance increases.,b:Drive faster because traction is better.,c:Visibility is always improved over pavement.
note: Loose surfaces reduce traction; slow down, allow more stopping distance, and avoid sudden maneuvers to prevent skids.

question: Which color are guide signs that provide directions and mileage information?
options: a:Green.,b:Yellow.,c:Red.
note: Guide or destination signs are green and provide directional and distance information.

question: When parking downhill on a two-way road with no curb, which way should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Turn the wheels toward the right (toward the side of the road).,b:Turn the wheels straight ahead.,c:Turn the wheels left toward the center of the road.
note: Parking downhill with no curb, turn the wheels toward the roadside so the vehicle would roll away from traffic if brakes fail.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing a vehicle going the same direction, when is it safe to return to the right lane?
options: a:When you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror,b:After approximately three seconds,c:When you can no longer see the passed vehicle over your right shoulder
note: Return to your lane only after seeing the passed vehicle’s headlights in your rearview mirror and checking blind spots.

question: What does a single dashed white centerline between lanes indicate?
options: a:Lanes move in the same direction and you may pass/change lanes if safe.,b:Lanes move in opposite directions and passing is prohibited.,c:You are not allowed to pass under any condition.
note: Dashed white lines separate same-direction lanes and may be crossed to pass or change lanes when safe.

question: After passing another vehicle, when is it safe to merge back into the original lane?
options: a:When you cannot see the vehicle to your right.,b:When you can see the passed vehicle’s headlights in your rearview mirror.,c:When you are one vehicle length ahead of it.,d:After 50 feet.
note: Return to your lane only after you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror, indicating you have sufficient space.

question: To help prevent crashes, you should:
options: a:Communicate intent to other road users (signals, brake lights, horn when needed),b:Ignore other drivers and focus only on your lane,c:Drive only on side streets
note: Communicating with signals and other cues lets others anticipate your actions and reduces crash risk.

question: Why should you avoid making sudden stops in front of large trucks or buses?
options: a:Because large vehicles require longer distances to stop and may not be able to avoid a collision,b:Because large vehicles always travel faster than cars,c:Because smaller vehicles cannot see trucks' brake lights
note: Large vehicles need more distance to stop; sudden stops in front of them can cause rear-end collisions.

question: To avoid hydroplaning in heavy rain you should:
options: a:Reduce your speed,b:Use cruise control at a constant speed,c:Immediately move to the shoulder when the rain starts
note: Lower your speed in wet conditions to reduce the chance your tires will ride on a film of water.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Interstate driving requires drivers to:
options: a:Be constantly alert and able to safely drive at increased speeds,b:Only drive at posted minimum speeds,c:Use cruise control at all times
note: Using the interstate safely requires constant alertness and the ability to safely operate at higher speeds.

question: If you start to feel drowsy while driving, what is the safest action?
options: a:Stop, rest, or change drivers.,b:Drink caffeinated beverages to keep driving.,c:Open the window and keep driving.
note: To avoid fatigued driving, stop to rest or switch drivers. Short measures like caffeine or windows are not reliable.

question: What should you do with your following distance when driving on slippery roads?
options: a:Increase your following distance to allow more stopping time.,b:Keep the same following distance as on dry roads.,c:Decrease your following distance to keep traffic flowing.,d:Follow closer to use the other vehicle as a windbreak.
note: Slippery conditions increase stopping distance, so you should increase the space between you and the vehicle ahead.

question: From a center left-turn lane, which maneuvers are typically permitted?
options: a:Making left turns only.,b:Passing slow traffic in either direction.,c:Driving straight through the intersection.,d:Making U-turns only during right-of-way gaps.
note: A center lane reserved for left turns from either direction is for left turns only; it is not for passing or through traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection simultaneously, which driver must yield?
options: a:The driver of the larger vehicle.,b:The driver on the right.,c:The driver on the left.,d:The driver who honks first.
note: If two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left should yield to the driver on the right; the driver on the left yields and proceeds when safe.

question: If a child is about to run into the street in front of your vehicle, what action should you take immediately?
options: a:Begin preparing to slow down and sound a sharp blast of your horn if needed.,b:Flash your headlights.,c:Drive around the child.,d:Ignore and continue at the same speed.
note: If a child is about to run into the street, prepare to slow and, if necessary, use a sharp horn blast to warn them and other drivers.

question: When is it permissible to stop or park along the shoulder of a freeway?
options: a:Only in an emergency or when directed by authorities.,b:Whenever you need to check a map.,c:If you turn on your hazard lights and the vehicle is off the road.,d:Any time there is no traffic present.
note: Parking on a freeway shoulder is prohibited except for emergencies or when directed by officials.

question: How do worn or bald tires affect driving?
options: a:They can increase stopping distance and raise hydroplaning risk,b:They always decrease fuel consumption,c:They improve traction in wet conditions
note: Tires with inadequate tread can increase stopping distances, make turning harder, and increase the chance of hydroplaning.

question: Which of the following does NOT affect your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:The type of alcoholic beverage you drink.,b:Your body weight.,c:How much time passes between drinks.
note: BAC is influenced by amount consumed, time between drinks, and body weight; the beverage type does not change BAC.

question: Is it legal to cross a double solid yellow centerline to pass?
options: a:No — you may not pass over double solid yellow lines.,b:Yes; it's always allowed.,c:Yes, only if no oncoming traffic is present.
note: Two solid yellow lines mean no passing from either direction, except to turn into a driveway or private road.

question: Why is extra space needed in front of large trucks?
options: a:So the truck has room to stop safely due to its greater stopping distance,b:So other drivers can merge behind the truck,c:So trucks can accelerate faster
note: Trucks need extra stopping distance due to their size and weight; do not pull in front of them then slow down.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When a vehicle is merging onto the freeway from an entrance ramp, how should you react if you are on the freeway?
options: a:Make room by changing lanes or adjusting speed to allow a smooth merge.,b:Speed up aggressively to keep your position.,c:Ignore them — you have the right-of-way.
note: Help merging traffic by changing lanes or easing up to create a gap so they can enter safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you NOT forget to do when changing lanes?
options: a:Check mirrors and blind spots and use your turn signal.,b:Only check your rearview mirror.,c:Assume no other drivers are nearby so signaling is unnecessary.
note: Before changing lanes, check side and rearview mirrors, look over your shoulder for blind spots, and signal your intention.

question: A pentagon-shaped sign is used to indicate:
options: a:A school zone or school crossing area,b:A stop sign,c:A regulatory instruction
note: Five-sided (pentagon) signs alert drivers to school zones and school crossings where children may be present.

question: When driving in bad weather, what should you do about following distance?
options: a:Increase your following distance.,b:Decrease your following distance.,c:Maintain the same following distance as normal.,d:Follow closer to avoid others cutting in.
note: Increase following distance in adverse weather to allow more time to react if the vehicle ahead stops suddenly.

question: What do circular road signs typically warn of?
options: a:School zones.,b:Railroad crossings ahead.,c:No passing zones.,d:Stop requirements ahead.
note: Round signs warn drivers that a railroad crossing is coming; exercise extra caution when you approach.

question: When a vehicle with ABS loses traction on a slippery road, you should:
options: a:Press and hold the brake pedal,b:Pump the brakes,c:Let up on the brake and reapply repeatedly
note: With Anti-Lock Braking Systems, press and hold the brake pedal firmly; the ABS will pump the brakes automatically.

question: If your vehicle's right wheels leave the pavement, you should:
options: a:Ease off the accelerator, steer parallel to the road, slow, then carefully steer back onto the pavement,b:Brake sharply and jerk the wheel back onto the road,c:Immediately accelerate to get back onto the pavement quickly
note: If your right wheels leave the pavement, slow down, steer parallel to the road, then steer back on cautiously when safe.

question: What do orange construction signs indicate?
options: a:Construction or maintenance activity ahead,b:A no passing zone,c:A bus stop ahead
note: Orange signs are used for construction, maintenance, and emergency operation warnings.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If the centerline has one solid yellow line and one broken yellow line and the broken line is next to your lane, what does that mean?
options: a:You may pass from your lane if it is safe to do so.,b:You may not pass in this area.,c:You may only make right turns from this lane.
note: When the broken line is on your side, passing is permitted from your lane if no oncoming traffic is present and it's safe.

question: Turning your head to check a blind spot before changing lanes is:
options: a:A good driving habit,b:A bad driving habit,c:Unnecessary if mirrors are adjusted
note: Checking blind spots by looking over your shoulder is a good habit and should be done when changing lanes or merging.

question: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights and/or siren approaches, you should:
options: a:Pull over to the right and stop until it passes,b:Speed up and try to reach your destination first,c:Continue driving but try to stay out of its way
note: Yield right-of-way to emergency vehicles by pulling to the right edge of the road and stopping until they pass.

question: How should you approach a railroad crossing that has no active signals?
options: a:Always stop even if no train is visible.,b:Slow down and be prepared to stop if needed.,c:Assume there will always be signals and proceed normally.,d:Honk continuously while crossing.
note: Approach an unprotected crossing with caution: slow down, look and listen for trains, and be prepared to stop if you see or hear one.

question: What does a double solid yellow centerline mean about passing?
options: a:Passing is allowed from both directions.,b:Passing is allowed only from your side.,c:Passing is not allowed from either direction.,d:Passing is permitted at any time at the driver's discretion.
note: Double solid yellow lines indicate that passing across the centerline is prohibited for traffic in both directions.

question: A sign reading 'Reduced speed, 35 mph' means what regarding the new limit?
options: a:The reduced 35 mph speed limit begins at that sign.,b:The new limit begins at the next posted speed sign.,c:You have plenty of time after the sign to slow down gradually.
note: A posted reduced speed sign indicates the new limit takes effect at that sign and must be obeyed from that point.

question: If your vehicle's wheels have run off the pavement onto the shoulder, what is the best initial action?
options: a:Hold the steering wheel firmly, ease off the gas, and gently apply the brakes.,b:Turn the front wheels sharply to the left and brake hard.,c:Turn the front wheels slightly left to edge back onto pavement immediately.
note: If you leave the roadway, grip the wheel firmly, lift off the accelerator, brake gently, reduce speed, check traffic, and re-enter when safe. Sudden steering can cause loss of control.

question: Why should you look farther ahead on a freeway compared to a city street?
options: a:To spot potential hazards and changes in traffic earlier.,b:Because freeways always require slower speeds.,c:Because signals change less frequently.,d:To avoid using your mirrors.
note: On a freeway you need to watch traffic flow and hazards further ahead to allow time to react to merging vehicles and rapid changes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to pass another vehicle, which assumption is safe to make?
options: a:Do not assume the other driver will provide space for you to return to your lane,b:Assume the other driver will maintain a constant speed,c:Assume using your signal guarantees the other driver will let you pass
note: Never assume other drivers will make room or maintain their speed; always ensure it is safe before passing.

question: Is it true that double solid yellow lines allow passing from either direction?
options: a:FALSE,b:TRUE,c:Only at night.,d:Only if the road is empty.
note: Double solid yellow lines prohibit passing from either direction except for permitted left turns or to pass non-motorized road users when safe and legal.

question: What does a green arrow above a reversible lane indicate?
options: a:Drivers may use that lane as indicated.,b:The lane is about to close with a red X.,c:Drivers should not enter this lane under any circumstance.,d:The lane is only for emergency vehicles.
note: A green arrow means the lane is open and you may use it as shown by the signal.

question: What road marking or sign is commonly used to direct drivers into the correct lane for turning?
options: a:Arrows painted on the pavement or lane-control arrows.,b:Flashing red lights on the side of the road.,c:White lines on the side of the road only.,d:Crosswalk markings.
note: Arrows indicate which lanes are designated for turning or for going straight and help drivers position their vehicles correctly.

question: Which is an appropriate time to use your horn?
options: a:To greet a friend on the sidewalk.,b:When a bicyclist is riding carefully.,c:If you lose control of your vehicle and need to warn others.,d:To express irritation at slow drivers.
note: Use your horn to warn others of danger — for example, if you lose control of your car — not for greetings or anger.

question: A broken yellow centerline indicates that:
options: a:Passing is not permitted.,b:Passing on the left is permitted when the way ahead is clear.,c:Passing on the right is permitted only.,d:Traffic moves in the same direction on both sides.
note: A broken yellow line next to your lane means you may pass to the left when it is safe and clear of oncoming traffic.

question: If a tire suddenly goes flat while driving, what is the correct response?
options: a:Brake hard and immediately pull to the side.,b:Hold the steering wheel firmly, ease off the accelerator, and gradually slow down.,c:Turn off the ignition suddenly.,d:Speed up to reach the shoulder faster.
note: Grip the steering wheel, stay straight, take your foot off the accelerator and allow the vehicle to slow gradually; brake gently only if necessary and pull off when safe.

question: If a fire engine is following you but is not using lights or siren, what should you do?
options: a:Stop as quickly as possible.,b:Continue driving normally.,c:Speed up to get out of the way.,d:Pull over immediately to the right shoulder.
note: If an emergency vehicle is not using emergency signals, you should continue driving normally; you only clear the way when lights/siren are active.

question: What does a curb painted red signify?
options: a:Loading zone for deliveries.,b:Area reserved for passenger pick-up and drop-off.,c:No parking, standing, or stopping.,d:Handicap parking only.
note: A red-painted curb means no stopping, standing, or parking is allowed in that area.

question: If there is an oncoming car to your left and a bicyclist to your right, how should you handle passing the bicyclist?
options: a:Split the difference and pass between them.,b:Let the oncoming car pass first, then pass the bicyclist.,c:Pull onto the shoulder and pass both.,d:Pass the bicyclist first while the oncoming car slows.
note: When there are multiple hazards, handle one at a time: let the oncoming car pass, then pass the bicyclist when it is safe to do so.

question: A downward-pointing triangular sign typically means:
options: a:Yield,b:School zone,c:Construction ahead
note: A downward-facing triangular sign generally tells drivers to yield until it is safe to proceed.

question: On slippery roads, how should your following distance change?
options: a:Increase the following distance (leave more space than normal).,b:Keep the same distance as normal.,c:Follow more closely than normal.
note: Slippery conditions require a longer stopping distance; increase your following gap accordingly.

question: If you start to feel tired while driving, what's the best action?
options: a:Stop driving and rest,b:Open a window and play loud music,c:Drink coffee and continue driving
note: Fatigue impairs driving similar to alcohol; stop driving and rest if you become tired.

question: Alcohol in any concentration is classified as:
options: a:A depressant,b:A stimulant,c:Neither of the above
note: Alcohol is a depressant that slows nerve impulses and impairs driving-related skills.

question: What is the proper term for the measurement of alcohol in the bloodstream?
options: a:Implied consent (IC).,b:Blood alcohol concentration (BAC).,c:Rate of alcohol consumption (RAC).,d:Alcohol impairment quotient (AIQ).
note: Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) measures the percentage of alcohol in a person's bloodstream; higher BAC means greater impairment.

question: How is defensive driving best defined?
options: a:Identifying dangerous driving situations and taking action to avoid accidents.,b:Getting ahead in traffic by aggressive maneuvers.,c:Following other vehicles closely to anticipate their moves.,d:Relying on other drivers to follow the rules.
note: Defensive driving means anticipating hazards and taking proactive measures to prevent crashes.

question: When entering an interstate, after locating a gap and signaling you should:
options: a:Expect traffic to pull over for you.,b:Merge carefully into the gap when it is safe.,c:Wait for every lane to clear completely before merging.,d:Stop at the lane's end and then enter traffic.
note: Identify a gap, match the speed of traffic, signal, and merge carefully into the gap when safe; do not assume others will yield.

question: If you must stop along the road at night, what lights should remain on?
options: a:Turn off all lights so you are not seen.,b:Use parking lights only.,c:Keep low-beam headlights and emergency flashers on.,d:Only leave interior lights on.
note: If you stop at night, turn on your emergency flashers and leave your low-beam headlights on so other motorists can see you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a flashing red traffic light require you to do?
options: a:Come to a complete stop and proceed when safe, same as a stop sign.,b:Slow down and proceed with caution.,c:Prepare for the light to turn green.
note: A flashing red light has the same meaning as a stop sign: stop, yield, and proceed when clear.

question: What important characteristic of large trucks should passenger vehicle drivers be aware of?
options: a:They have large blind spots and need more room to maneuver and stop.,b:They can stop much quicker than passenger vehicles.,c:They always travel at the posted speed limit.,d:They never cause wind gusts when passing.
note: Large trucks have extensive blind spots and require more distance to maneuver and stop; avoid lingering beside or too close behind them.

question: If your power steering suddenly fails while driving, what should you do first?
options: a:Work hard to steer, slow down, move to a safe area, and stop.,b:Honk your horn and turn off the ignition.,c:Turn on your hazard lights and brace yourself.
note: If power steering stops, more physical effort is required to control the vehicle. Reduce speed, steer carefully to a safe place off the road, and stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When a green arrow is displayed at an intersection, what must a driver do?
options: a:Proceed in the arrow's direction after yielding to any vehicles, bicycles, or pedestrians still in the intersection.,b:Ignore pedestrians and only watch for vehicles.,c:Wait four seconds before turning.,d:Treat it the same as a circular green light with no restrictions.
note: A green arrow indicates you may go in the direction shown, but you must first yield to any vehicles, bicycles, or pedestrians still in the intersection.

question: When passing a large truck, what should the driver of a small vehicle be prepared for?
options: a:Wind gusts that may affect the smaller vehicle's stability.,b:Complete silence because trucks are very quiet.,c:That there will be no air turbulence at freeway speeds.,d:That the truck will always slow down for you.
note: Large vehicles can produce strong air turbulence; small vehicles should be prepared to correct steering when passing or being passed.

question: When parking uphill next to a curb, how should you set your wheels?
options: a:Turn your steering wheel away from the curb and set the parking brake.,b:Keep your front tires straight and do not use the parking brake.,c:Turn your steering wheel toward the curb so the vehicle will roll into it.,d:Turn the wheels sharply to the right and leave the car in neutral.
note: When parked uphill with a curb, turn the wheels away from the curb and set the parking brake so the vehicle will roll into the curb if it moves.

question: If other drivers nearby are acting angrily, what should you do?
options: a:Distance yourself from them and avoid eye contact or gestures.,b:Make eye contact and match their behavior.,c:React with hand gestures to show you are right.
note: Physically and mentally distance yourself from aggressive drivers; avoid gestures or eye contact that could provoke them.

question: Which best describes the mindset of defensive drivers?
options: a:Anticipating what other drivers might do and preparing to react safely.,b:Assuming other drivers will always follow the rules.,c:Driving aggressively to get ahead of poor drivers.,d:Never yielding the right-of-way.
note: Defensive drivers expect that others may make mistakes and take actions to avoid crashes.

question: True or false: Your speed does not affect how far your vehicle travels after you apply the brakes.
options: a:True,b:False,c:Only on dry roads,d:Only when you have anti-lock brakes
note: As speed increases, stopping distance increases. Faster driving means it will take longer and farther to stop.

question: If your car breaks down on a highway, what should you do to warn others and ensure safety?
options: a:Signal, move off the traveled way, and turn on your four-way flashers.,b:Stay in the center lane and wait for help.,c:Sound your horn continuously to alert motorists.
note: When disabled, carefully get off the road, use hazard flashers, and park where other drivers can see you. Raise your hood to indicate trouble.

question: When should you allow an extra cushion of space around your vehicle?
options: a:When following a driver who cannot see the rear of their vehicle (such as a truck with a trailer).,b:When following a small passenger car only.,c:When driving at the posted speed limit in clear weather.,d:Only when driving on residential streets.
note: Give extra following distance behind large vehicles that may not be able to see you or that block your view of the road ahead.

question: Is it ever acceptable to leave the scene of a collision because it doesn't look serious?
options: a:FALSE,b:TRUE,c:Only if the owner isn't present.,d:Only on private property.
note: You must not leave the scene of a collision. Failing to stop and provide contact or information can result in hit-and-run charges.

question: A red flashing traffic light is equivalent to which traffic control device?
options: a:A stop sign — come to a complete stop.,b:A yield sign.,c:A steady red light.
note: A flashing red signal has the same meaning as a stop sign: stop, yield, and proceed when safe.

question: Does drinking coffee reduce your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:No — coffee does not affect BAC.,b:Yes — it reduces BAC.,c:Yes — it cancels the alcohol's effects.
note: Coffee may make you feel more alert, but it does not change your BAC or sober you up.

question: Before starting the engine, what safety step should you take?
options: a:Buckle your safety belt and ensure passengers are buckled,b:Only have backseat passengers buckled,c:Only ensure adult passengers are buckled
note: Make it a routine to buckle your seat belt and ensure all passengers are buckled before switching on the ignition.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When an emergency vehicle is using its siren or flashing lights, what must you do?
options: a:Keep driving normally and do not change lanes.,b:Yield the right-of-way and allow it to pass.,c:Speed up to get out of its way.,d:Stop immediately in your lane and remain there.
note: You must yield the right-of-way to police, fire, ambulances, and other emergency vehicles using sirens or flashing lights; follow any instructions from their loudspeakers and clear the way safely.

question: If you have had several beers, how can their effects be reduced?
options: a:Only by waiting several hours for your body to process the alcohol,b:By taking a cold shower,c:By drinking coffee
note: The impairing effects of alcohol are only reduced by allowing time for your body to eliminate it.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are already in an intersection when the traffic light turns yellow, what should you do?
options: a:Continue through and clear the intersection safely.,b:Stop immediately in the middle of the intersection.,c:Speed up to beat the red light at all costs.,d:Back up to the previous intersection.
note: If you entered the intersection on green and the light turns yellow, clear it promptly and safely rather than stopping in it.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you obey instructions from school crossing guards?
options: a:At all times when they are directing traffic.,b:Only during official school hours.,c:Only if you see children present.
note: Drivers must always obey crossing guards' instructions when they are directing traffic near schools.

question: If an oncoming vehicle is heading toward you in your lane, what should you do first?
options: a:Blow your horn, steer right, and brake,b:Blow your horn, steer left, and accelerate,c:Blow your horn, steer right, and brake
note: If another vehicle is approaching head-on in your lane, honk to attract attention, try to move right, and brake firmly if collision seems unavoidable.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: True or false: The posted maximum speed limit is always the safest speed to drive.
options: a:True,b:False,c:Only on highways,d:Only in good weather
note: The posted limit is the maximum legal speed under ideal conditions; you must drive slower when conditions (weather, visibility, traffic) require it.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You should not pass another vehicle in which situations?
options: a:On a hill or curve, at intersections, or when a school bus's red lights are flashing,b:Only when a car is going faster than you,c:Always pass on narrow bridges
note: Never pass on hills, curves, at intersections, or where visibility is limited; do not pass a stopped school bus with flashing red lights.

question: To safely pass a bicyclist, what is the recommended method?
options: a:Honk to alert them immediately.,b:Drive into the bicycle lane to pass.,c:Slow down and give as much space as possible when passing.,d:Pass quickly with minimal lateral distance.
note: When passing a bicyclist, slow down and leave as much room as you can to avoid crowding them or causing them to swerve.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A green traffic arrow indicates:
options: a:You must yield to oncoming traffic before turning.,b:You may proceed in the arrow direction after yielding to vehicles/pedestrians in the intersection.,c:The same as a circular green with no restriction.,d:That turning is prohibited.
note: A green arrow allows movement in the indicated direction but you must first yield to any vehicles or pedestrians remaining in the intersection.

question: The term 'distracted driving' refers to:
options: a:Anything that takes your attention away from driving,b:Anything that causes you to focus more on driving,c:Only texting while driving
note: Distracted driving includes any activity that diverts attention from driving, increasing crash risk.

question: If an oncoming vehicle has high beams on at night and it's hard for you to see, where should you look?
options: a:Toward the right edge of your lane and use peripheral vision.,b:Toward the centerline of the road.,c:Directly at the headlights to judge position.
note: Avoid looking at the bright light; glance to the right edge of the road and watch the vehicle using peripheral vision.

question: A driver should pay attention to which areas around their vehicle?
options: a:Beside, ahead, and to the rear of the car,b:Only directly in front of the car,c:Only in the rearview mirror
note: A good driver scans ahead, to the sides, and behind to be aware of the driving environment.

question: When a school bus stopped ahead has its lights flashing and stop arm extended, you must:
options: a:Slow down and pass carefully.,b:Stop until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn.,c:Change lanes and continue at the same speed.,d:Honk to alert the bus driver you are present.
note: If a school bus is stopped with flashing red lights and stop arm out, you must stop and wait until the lights are off and the stop arm is withdrawn before proceeding.

question: If an oncoming driver fails to dim high beams, where should you look?
options: a:Toward the right side of the road to avoid being blinded.,b:Toward the centerline to judge distance.,c:Straight ahead at all times.
note: Look to the right edge of the road and use peripheral vision to keep your vehicle on course without being blinded.

question: What can happen when alcohol is combined with another drug?
options: a:The effects of both substances may be increased, producing greater impairment.,b:They will cancel each other out and have no effect.,c:Both effects will always decrease.,d:Only the alcohol will have an effect.
note: Combining alcohol with other drugs can amplify effects, increasing impairment beyond what either would cause alone.

question: Who is required to wear a seat belt under Oklahoma law?
options: a:Every front-seat occupant and children under 13 regardless of seating position.,b:Only the driver.,c:Only occupants under 13 years old.
note: Oklahoma law requires all front-seat occupants to wear seat belts; children under 13 must be secured regardless of seating position.

question: True or false: A motorist turning left must yield to an oncoming bicyclist just like they would yield to an oncoming vehicle.
options: a:True,b:False,c:Only if the bicyclist is on the sidewalk.,d:Only if signs indicate to yield to bicycles
note: When turning left, yield to oncoming bicycles the same as you would to oncoming motor vehicles.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If another driver passes you in a no-passing zone, what should you do?
options: a:Pull off the road.,b:Maintain your speed and lane position.,c:Slow down to let the other driver safely return to the lane.,d:Speed up to prevent them from cutting in.
note: If you are being illegally passed, reduce speed slightly and allow the passing vehicle to move back into the lane safely.

question: If you see a pedestrian with a guide dog or white cane, you must:
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to them,b:Proceed as usual; they must yield,c:Flash your lights to make them aware
note: Drivers must yield the right-of-way to blind or partially blind pedestrians using a guide dog or white cane.

question: A single dashed yellow line between opposing lanes indicates:
options: a:Drivers may pass if it is safe to do so.,b:Both lanes travel in the same direction.,c:Passing is prohibited.,d:This lane is for bicycles only.
note: A single dashed yellow centerline means traffic in both directions may pass when it is safe and legal to do so.

question: When must you stop for a school bus on a two-lane highway?
options: a:When the bus is stopped with red lights flashing and/or its stop arm extended,b:Only if the bus is stopped in your lane,c:Only if children are visible crossing the road
note: On two-lane roads, traffic in both directions must stop for a school bus that has flashing red lights and/or an extended stop arm.

question: What does a steady yellow X above a reversible lane tell drivers?
options: a:The lane is about to close; you should clear it.,b:The lane will soon change to a green arrow.,c:Drivers may continue to drive normally in that lane.,d:The lane is reserved for buses only.
note: A steady yellow X warns that the lane signal will change to a red X and you should move out of that lane.

question: If you hit an unattended parked vehicle and cannot find the owner, what must you do?
options: a:Leave a written note with your name, address, and accident details.,b:Do nothing more and drive away.,c:Wait at the scene until the police arrive regardless of circumstances.
note: If you cannot find the owner, leave a written notice with your contact details and the accident circumstances.

question: Temporary signs used in construction and maintenance areas usually have what colors?
options: a:Orange background with black writing,b:Red background with green writing,c:Yellow background with blue writing
note: Temporary work zone signs are orange with black letters or symbols.

question: Is it true that bridges and ramps can freeze before the main roadway?
options: a:TRUE,b:FALSE,c:Only on mountain roads.,d:Only at night.
note: Bridges and ramps are exposed to air on all sides and can become icy more quickly than the adjacent road surface; use extra caution.

question: When an authorized emergency vehicle using lights and/or sirens is approaching, you should:
options: a:Pull to the right edge of the roadway and stop until it passes.,b:Ignore and keep driving.,c:Speed up to stay ahead of it.
note: You must immediately pull to the right side of the road and stop to allow the emergency vehicle to pass safely.

question: True or false: Large vehicles can have blind spots extending up to 200 feet behind them.
options: a:True,b:False,c:Only for certain trucks,d:Only when towing trailers
note: Large commercial vehicles can have very large blind spots behind them; avoid tailgating as the driver may not see you.

question: When parking uphill on a two-way road with no curb, which direction should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Straight ahead.,b:Toward the side of the road (right).,c:Toward the center of the road (left).,d:Turn on hazard lights and leave wheels straight.
note: When parking on a hill without a curb (either uphill or downhill), turn the wheels toward the edge of the road so the vehicle will roll away from traffic if the brakes fail.

question: If a driver's left arm and hand are extended upward, what is that hand signal indicating?
options: a:Stopping.,b:Left turn.,c:Right turn.,d:Speeding up.
note: A left arm extended upward indicates the driver plans to turn right; know common hand signals and be prepared when following such vehicles.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you use your turn signal?
options: a:Any time you change lanes, pull into or out of a parking space, or enter traffic from a parking area or alley.,b:Only when making a U-turn.,c:Only when turning left at an intersection.,d:Never if no other vehicles are present.
note: You should signal for every intended lateral movement so other drivers are aware of your intentions.

question: When being tailgated, what should you do to reduce collision risk?
options: a:Increase the space in front of your vehicle and avoid sudden braking.,b:Brake suddenly to teach the tailgater a lesson.,c:Speed up to put distance between you and the tailgater.,d:Change lanes immediately without signaling.
note: If someone is tailgating, create extra space ahead of you and avoid sudden maneuvers; consider changing lanes safely to let them pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Passing is unlawful at which locations?
options: a:On hills, curves, intersections, and railroad crossings,b:Only on highways,c:Only when two lanes are present
note: Passing is unsafe and unlawful on hills, curves, intersections, and railroad crossings and other no-passing zones.

question: Which of the following does NOT occur after drinking alcohol?
options: a:You are less alert.,b:Your reflexes and reaction time speed up.,c:Your judgment of speed and distance becomes distorted.
note: Alcohol slows reaction time, reduces alertness, and distorts judgment of speed and distance; it does not speed up reflexes.

question: On average, how many standard alcoholic drinks does the body eliminate per hour?
options: a:Three drinks per hour.,b:One drink per hour.,c:Two drinks per hour.,d:None — alcohol accumulates indefinitely.
note: The average person's body metabolizes about one standard drink per hour, though many factors affect actual impairment and processing time.

question: What helps you avoid the need for emergency stops in traffic?
options: a:Looking ahead and keeping a safe following distance,b:Honing your horn frequently,c:Staying in the right lane only
note: Maintaining a safe following distance and scanning ahead lets you react to problems without sudden stops.

question: When driving near large trucks, what should other drivers allow for?
options: a:That large trucks require a longer stopping distance.,b:That large trucks produce less noise and are easier to hear.,c:That trucks always have smaller blind spots than cars.,d:That trucks can stop more quickly than passenger vehicles.
note: Large trucks need more room to stop and have large blind spots; smaller vehicles should stay where truck drivers can see them and avoid locations where the truck blocks their view of traffic.

question: What is the only thing that can lower blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Time,b:Eating fatty foods,c:Drinking coffee
note: Only time allows the body to metabolize alcohol and lower BAC; nothing else speeds this process.

question: Which of the following helps prevent hydroplaning?
options: a:Maintain good tire tread depth and proper inflation and reduce speed in rain,b:Always use cruise control,c:Drive in the shoulder if it starts to rain
note: Good tread and proper tire pressure, plus reduced speed in wet conditions, reduce hydroplaning risk.

question: At a railroad crossing with more than one track, after a train passes you should:
options: a:Proceed immediately as soon as the first train clears.,b:Wait until you can see down all tracks and be sure no other trains are coming.,c:Cross while watching for oncoming cars.,d:Honk before crossing to alert any other trains.
note: After a train passes, wait until you have a clear view of all tracks and are sure no other trains are approaching before crossing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the most common cause of traffic crashes?
options: a:Human error (driver mistakes).,b:Bad weather.,c:New drivers.
note: Most crashes occur because of human error — failing to see other vehicles or unpredictable driver actions.

question: Drowsy drivers may:
options: a:Drive poorly and appear intoxicated,b:Drive better than usual,c:Always be alert after drinking coffee
note: Drowsiness can impair driving so severely that it resembles intoxication; coffee or radio may not fix it.

question: Under normal driving conditions, what is the minimum following distance you should maintain?
options: a:One second.,b:Two seconds.,c:Three seconds.,d:Four seconds.
note: Keep a minimum three-second following distance under normal conditions; increase it in poor weather or heavy traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left onto a one-way street, into which lane should you turn?
options: a:Into the lane closest to your original lane (usually the leftmost lane).,b:Into the rightmost lane on the one-way street.,c:Into any lane as long as you signal.,d:Into the lane farthest from your original lane.
note: Always turn from the lane nearest the direction you wish to go into the first available legal lane on the street you enter.

question: How do you check your blind spot before changing lanes?
options: a:Look over your shoulder toward the direction you plan to move.,b:Look only in the left side mirror.,c:Check the rearview mirror only.
note: Look over your shoulder toward the lane you intend to enter to cover the blind spot not visible in mirrors.

question: What is the best way to avoid alcohol-related crashes?
options: a:Decide before you begin drinking that you will not drive and arrange alternate transportation.,b:Say 'No thanks, I'm driving' only when offered a drink.,c:Call a taxi only if you feel very intoxicated.
note: Deciding ahead of time not to drive and arranging alternative transportation is the most reliable way to avoid drunk driving.

question: When driving in snow or ice you should:
options: a:Make speed and directional changes more gradually and avoid using cruise control,b:Use cruise control to maintain steady speed,c:Drive as you would in normal conditions
note: On snow or ice, make slower, smoother steering and speed changes; never use cruise control in these conditions.

question: To improve visibility in rain or fog, drivers should use:
options: a:Low-beam headlights,b:High-beam headlights,c:Parking lights only
note: Use low-beam headlights in rain or fog; high beams can reflect back and reduce visibility.

question: After stopping for a train at a crossing, what should you check for before proceeding?
options: a:Only that the gates are up.,b:Look for a second train and ensure all warning signals have stopped.,c:That the first train cleared the nearest track regardless of other tracks.,d:Only that no cars are behind you.
note: Wait until all trains have cleared, all gates are lifted, and warning signals have stopped; watch for a second train on other tracks.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Should you enter an intersection if doing so will leave you blocking it when the light turns red?
options: a:No — never enter unless you can clear the intersection completely.,b:Yes — if you entered on a yellow light.,c:Yes — if you entered on a green light.
note: Even on green, do not enter an intersection unless you can clear it before the light turns red; blocking intersections can result in citations.

question: Why is driving at night more dangerous than during daylight?
options: a:You cannot see as far ahead at night due to reduced visibility and headlight glare.,b:The road surface is always more slippery at night.,c:Your reaction time is always slower at night.,d:Traffic laws are less enforced at night.
note: Reduced visibility and glare from headlights limit how far ahead you can see, making night driving more hazardous.

question: If you are emotionally upset from an incident at work, what should you do before driving?
options: a:Take a few minutes to cool off before you begin driving home.,b:Turn the radio up loudly to distract yourself.,c:Drive fast to let off steam on the road.
